title: Vecchia_approximation
summary: The Vecchia approximation is a Gaussian processes approximation technique originally developed by Aldo Vecchia, a statistician at the United States Geological Survey. It is one of the earliest attempts to use Gaussian processes in high-dimensional settings. The approximation replaces the high-dimensional joint distribution with a product of univariate conditional distributions, conditioning on only a small subset of previous observations, leading to a sparse Cholesky factor of the precision matrix. This reduces computational complexity to O(nk^3). Katzfuss and Guinness (2021) proposed a general framework in Statistical Science that contains many popular existing GP approximations as special cases. Software implementations include GPvecchia, GpGp (R packages on CRAN), and GPBoost (C++ library with Python and R interfaces).
